subject: Behavioral Economics
title: Libertarian Paternalism
description: A quick, practical guide to Libertarian Paternalism.

hook.text: Can you steer someone toward better choices without limiting their freedom? Thaler says yes.

buildup.text: Libertarian: all options stay available. Paternalism: the default option is the one that helps you most.

discovery.text: Auto-enrolling employees in retirement plans is libertarian paternalism. They can opt out. Almost nobody does.

twist.text: Critics say any default is a choice made for you. But no default is also a design choice: doing nothing is a nudge too.

climax.text: Every choice environment has an architecture. The only question is: is it designed well or by accident?

punchline.text: No design is neutral. So design wisely.

quiz.question: What does libertarian paternalism mean?
options: Removing all choices and deciding for people
Steering people toward better choices while preserving freedom
Letting people figure everything out alone

details.summary: Libertarian paternalism is the philosophical foundation of nudge theory, arguing that it is both legitimate and desirable to influence behavior while respecting freedom of choice. Choice architects should steer people toward better decisions while ensuring they can always choose otherwise.
details.whyItMatters: Libertarian paternalism resolves the tension between wanting to help people make better choices and respecting their autonomy. It provides the ethical framework for nudges by insisting that interventions must preserve choice while guiding the.
takeaways: Nudges influence behavior while preserving complete freedom to choose otherwise
Choice architecture is never neutral, so designers must choose a direction
The standard is what fully informed, deliberate individuals would choose for themselves

faq.question: How can something be both libertarian and paternalistic?
faq.answer: Libertarian means choice is preserved: nobody is forced. Paternalistic means the choice architect steers toward outcomes that are better for the chooser. The combination guides without mandating. You are nudged toward more savings but never forced to save.

faq.question: What are the strongest criticisms of libertarian paternalism?
faq.answer: Critics argue that it disguises paternalism in libertarian language, that defaults are so powerful they effectively remove choice, that choice architects may not know what is best for individuals, and that it is a slippery slope toward harder paternalism.
